title: How to stop tearing calluses (handcare for lifters)
summary: Hand care routine for lifters to stop tearing calluses. Chalk dries the skin, so he moisturizes nightly with a climbers' balm, and he shaves calluses flat with a nail clipper every two weeks so the bar has no ridge to catch. He also shows how to trim the loose skin around a palm split so it heals faster.

claims.claim: Torn calluses and skin cuts can stop you from training even when the rest of your body is healthy, because you can't grip the bar.
Calluses tear and skin cracks because chalk absorbs the skin's moisture, not just sweat; washing the chalk off afterwards is not enough.
Lifters who use chalk should apply a moisturizing product to their hands every day; he uses Climb On, a fatty balm made for rock climbers.
Apply the hand balm right before bed because it makes hands greasy; it takes about 6-7 hours to absorb, so it is gone by morning.
Calluses are good because they protect the hand, but bulky ones form ridges the bar can catch and rip off, taking deep live skin with them and ending the session.
Cut your calluses with a nail clipper every two weeks, the day before a rest day.
Since he started shaving his calluses he has never ripped one; before, it happened about every three weeks and drove him crazy.
Some skin splits from aggressive knurling can't be avoided; they take about a week to heal and happen much more when he gets lazy about nightly hand hydration.
Cut calluses right after training when they are bulky, never after a shower, because softened skin makes you cut too deep.
To shave a callus, press the nail clipper into it and cut until completely flat; you only remove dead skin, so it neither hurts nor bleeds.
After shaving calluses you can lift normally two days later, and they grow back to the same size or bigger within two weeks.
The night you cut calluses, apply extra moisturizer before bed so it absorbs deeper and keeps the skin healthy longer.
For a split at the finger-palm crease, trim the loose flap of skin around it flat: the flap folds into the wound each time you close your hand and stops it healing.
If a hand split is too deep, he closes it with glue.
